When agents use this

Before choosing motion, then during slow playback, replay and interruption review.

Skills: jig-mockup, jig-verify, jig-review.

General UI stays under 300 ms; explanatory sequences have their own budget. The lab lets you experiment. Passing virtual time does not prove painted motion or comfort.

A real finding: The receipt appeared before arrival

Before: The coordinator’s motion-lab review found a transfer receipt appearing at 150 ms, before the arriving item had landed; its source was barely visible.

After / recorded fix: The recorded fix calls for showing the source first, using a visible path, and displaying the receipt after landing.

Why: Cause must precede effect. Slow playback and frame review catch this ordering error; passing final-state replay alone cannot.

Source: round-5 fix list, coordinator browser check, 7 Nov 2026

From README.md · Motion basics

Motion basics

Use this beside Craft basics, before building and during review. These are adaptations, not installed third-party skills. The person's decisions take precedence: explanatory sequences have their own budget, attention starts fast, and reduced motion retains gentle feedback. The coordinator's draft supplied the repeated-failure cases; its delayed gap closure is superseded by concurrent removal below. The source opportunity gate checks frequency, purpose, speed and function; here function is part of purpose and easing is an explicit question.

Briefs and motion ledgers use the motion vocabulary. When the person describes an effect loosely, the coordinator replies with its exact term and lab link before building. If no stage exists, disclose that gap and agree a lab comparison. Ordinary components use the motion recipes with project tokens and frequency decisions rather than new per-job motion.

CheckRuleSource
Four-question gateBefore proposing motion, answer in order: how often is it seen; what purpose does it serve and does it help the task; which easing fits; how fast can it finish? Reject candidates that delay reading or action.emil-design-eng; find-animation-opportunities, gate adapted
Frequency100+ uses/day: no animation; tens/day: remove or sharply reduce; occasional: standard; rare/first use: room for delight. Frequent shortcuts and palette toggles stay immediate.emil-design-eng
Two budgetsGeneral UI finishes under 300 ms: press 100–160 ms, tooltip/popover 125–200 ms, menu/select 150–250 ms, panel/drawer 200–299 ms. Explanatory cause-and-effect sequences may use 250–1250 ms, according to the person's chosen timings; do not stretch frequent UI to that budget.review-animations / STANDARDS; person, 8 Nov 2026 (overrides the source's 500 ms drawer upper bound)
ExitMake exits shorter and simpler than entrances; grouped exits happen together, without reverse staggering.choreograph; emil-design-eng
Easing tokensEnter and exit: cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1); on-screen move: cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1); drawer: cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1); hover: cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1) (the exact CSS ease curve); constant: linear. Never use ease-in for UI.review-animations / STANDARDS, hover keyword expanded to its curve
Scale and originNever enter from scale(0); start near full size (0.9–0.97) with opacity. Anchor transform-origin to the trigger; centred modals keep their centre.emil-design-eng
PropertiesAnimate only transform, opacity and drawing properties such as stroke-dashoffset or clip-path. Change layout once, then animate transforms; never tween width, height, margins, padding, top or left. Drawing can still paint: inspect its frame cost.review-animations / STANDARDS; emil-design-eng, drawing exception; coordinator draft
Explicit transitionsName each transitioned property; never use transition: all.review-animations
Collapse and removalAt removal, take the leaving object out of layout immediately (for example, absolute at its measured position). Its exit and its siblings closing the gap run together. Measure before/after layout and use inverted transforms for siblings; do not wait for a fade before closing the gap.choreograph; coordinator draft, revised
One object, one timingParts read as one object: an arrow's head and line, or a chip and label, share a start, duration and easing family. Move a parent when it should carry its parts.choreograph; coordinator draft
Cause then effectOrder only where it explains meaning. Start with second delay equal to first duration; then bring the handoff slightly early so it reads as one gesture, with the cause still legible. Independent motion runs together.choreograph
RolesAssign one lead, smaller/shorter support, decoration that only fades (or stays still), and static elements. Two competing leads need a hierarchy decision. If a panel enters, its children are already present.choreograph
StaggerUse 30–80 ms steps only for eligible occasional groups, finishing general UI under 300 ms. Never stagger frequent UI, and never block input while it plays. Long lists bring the rest in with the last staggered item.choreograph; review-animations / STANDARDS
InterruptionUse retargetable transitions or springs for rapid triggers. Stop in-flight work before starting another run; resume a chained sequence only after all reset animations complete. Test rapid repeat, reversal and replay for stale objects and timers.emil-design-eng; choreograph
Attention loopsFor a blocking item, start with a fast breath (about 0.9 s period) for the first few seconds, then one pulse about every 6 s. Pause during interaction, resume after reset, stop when seen (hovered, focused or opened). Keep an off switch; reduced motion uses a steady cue.choreograph, attention loops; person's choice, 8 Nov 2026, replaces the source's initial 2.5 s wait
Light and darkJudge equal noticeability in both modes. Tune light first; compensate through theme tokens for outline and halo strength rather than assuming identical values look equal.Person, 8 Nov 2026; coordinator draft (local addition, not a claim from a borrowed skill)
Reduced motionMake feedback gentler, not universally zero: remove travel, scale, stagger and loops; keep brief opacity feedback and permanent facts/receipts. Explanations can show successive still states.review-animations / STANDARDS; choreograph; person, 8 Nov 2026
HoverGate hover effects with @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) so a touch tap cannot trigger a false hover.emil-design-eng
Hidden tabsPause timers while the tab is hidden; do not consume a toast's reading time or accumulate unseen attention pulses. A lab may cancel and require explicit replay.emil-design-eng, Sonner principles
Review by framesInspect at 2–5× duration and frame by frame, then again with fresh eyes the next day. Check first beat, timing, origin, leftovers, replay and interruption; code or virtual-time checks do not establish feel. Ask: “would you still want it on the 50th use today?”review-animations / STANDARDS; choreograph; coordinator draft
Frame budgetDiagnose with a performance recording under realistic content and concurrent loading: about 16.7 ms/frame at 60 Hz and 8.3 ms at 120 Hz. Name layout, paint, main-thread work or compositing as the cause before fixing. A fast desktop or CPU throttling cannot prove a weaker GPU/device result.animation-performance
Driver under loadPrefer CSS or WAAPI for predetermined motion during navigation/loading; acceleration is conditional, not guaranteed by an API. Record the installed motion-library version and verify its accelerated path; layout/gesture callbacks may still use the main thread. Do not upgrade a dependency just to borrow a recipe.animation-performance
Per-frame workAvoid framework state updates per frame and inherited custom properties updated on large parents. Write transforms directly on the moving element; batch geometry reads before writes. Profile again as child counts grow. Static timing tokens are fine.animation-performance
Paint and layersProfile drawing, clipping, shadows and filters across target browsers; none is a guaranteed compositor-only path. Prefer fading a pre-rendered halo to animating a shadow. Keep animated blur below 20 px if used; add scoped, temporary will-change only for a measured problem and remove it when idle. Extra layers consume memory.animation-performance, conservative local adaptation

Motion reviews use one row per finding, with concrete values and its reason (review-animations):

BeforeAfterWhy
Exit holds a list gap until fading endsRemove from flow at exit start; siblings translate into place concurrentlyKeeps removal one gesture

Lab round: fix, reduce or cut

  1. Inventory the round's motion by component, file/line, driver, properties, token, frequency and purpose. Check purpose/frequency, easing/timing, physicality/origin, interruption, performance, accessibility, cohesion and missing explanatory changes. Re-read evidence and exclude documented choices before ranking by impact and effort. Sources: improve-animations and AUDIT.md.
  2. Give each candidate Keep, Fix, Reduce or Cut, with the deciding gate. Cut purposeless decoration, repeated data entrances and high-frequency delays; reduce frequent effects. Keep motion that explains a real change and the person's documented breathing/attention exceptions. A useful effect with bad easing or interruption gets a fix, not automatic deletion. Record useful effects deliberately kept as well as removals. Source: remove-animations.
  3. For each selected fix, write a bounded task with revision, ledger IDs, current evidence, exact target tokens and resolved values, affected files, scope limits, dependencies and mechanical/feel checks. Stay within the authorized round; do not turn a lab pass into a codebase audit. Source: improve-animations / PLAN-TEMPLATE.md.
  4. Before reducing/cutting, inspect hidden initial styles, completion callbacks, exit/unmount timing, focus transfers and layout shifts masked by FLIP. Remove obsolete waits with the motion; preserve final facts and immediate focus. Clean unused keyframes/imports only within scope; propose dependency removals separately. Replay rapid reversal, reduced motion, hidden-tab return and repeated runs. Report Before / After / Why and remaining visual/device gaps. Source: remove-animations.

From motion-lab/README.md

Motion lab

Generic motion stages with the toolbox house style. Open index.html from disk. Play and Replay rebuild every scene object and cancel outstanding animations and scheduled callbacks; speed changes reschedule remaining delays. Hidden stages and hidden tabs cancel work. Reduced motion preserves final facts and receipts.

The stage lifecycle, speed scheduler, cancellation, spring functions and Lucide icon geometry are copied and adapted from a local project's motion study dated 7 November 2026 (source index SHA-256: ef0f679bd4236a3fd63155a4c0b54ba515ac836ba033fad3a4b9c33ddf5af6a8). Source files were read only; project-specific sessions, tickets and hand-off scenes are excluded. Generic stages have been adapted to plain items, groups, panels and source/destination links. Lucide 0.468.0 geometry retains its ISC notice. Other extracted code remains under the repository's existing terms; no separate third-party licence was present in the local study.

Timing defaults live in tokens.css; the panel writes those same CSS custom properties. Per-stage speed scales animation and scheduler time. Framework helpers remain a classic script so file URLs need no server or module fetch. Projects may copy this framework and supply their own stages; neither project scenes nor project tokens belong here.

The shared duration tiers and easing curves now live in tokens.css. General UI defaults finish under 300 ms; the transfer scene uses the separate explanatory budget (250–1250 ms). The timing panel and speed slider deliberately allow experiments outside those defaults; they do not approve a production timing. The movement and drawer scenes select their own easing tokens, while constant transfers use linear. Reduced motion drops movement and drawing but keeps brief opacity feedback; transfer receipts remain without travelling dots. These practices are adapted from Emil Kowalski's emil-design-eng, review-animations/STANDARDS and choreograph; source links and the full MIT notice are retained in the toolbox attribution.

Run node check.cjs for virtual-time scene and replay checks. These cannot establish actual browser layout, paint, accessibility, animation feel or visual replay consistency. Those remain pending; no browser was launched.

The motion vocabulary links directly to named stages, including perimeter draw (event), halo (selection), breathing (real work), attention loop (blocking question) and FLIP collapse. Breathing simulates one event then stops at 30 seconds of silence; attention is a bounded 30-second preview, acknowledged by hover, focus or click. Stop all is the preview's pause control. Applications must also wire interaction pause/resume and settings, visibility and actual event activity. These guards are not an application engine.

Control recipes use tokens.css plus recipes.css and the optional recipes.mjs lifecycle adapters. They are tested separately with node --test tests/motion-recipes.test.mjs from the repository root. The new stages and adapters remain prototypes pending rendered and feel review.

From README.md · Borrowed practices and attribution

Borrowed practices and attribution

Selected practices and rule logic adapted from Paul Bakaus's Impeccable, Apache-2.0, pinned to 924bbd194d02e5e15a227e75b5901fb0d7a4ecad (read 8 November 2026). Copyright 2025 Paul Bakaus. The complete upstream licence is retained in IMPECCABLE-LICENSE.txt.

Files adapted: PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, skill/reference/init.md and document.md inform the brief; bolder.md, quieter.md, polish.md, typeset.md, layout.md, colorize.md, delight.md, distill.md, clarify.md, harden.md, critique.md and audit.md inform the feedback vocabulary. These are rewritten in jig's words with confirmed/open distinctions, linked authoritative tokens, explicit desktop/input/density context, curated taste reactions, scoped guardrails and the person's tweak-bar requirement. No commands or interviews are installed.

crates/core/src/checks/rules.rs (is_card_like_from_props, check_icon_tile, glow gates), css_scan.rs (radial halo), measures.rs (radial spotlight), crates/html/src/page.rs (nested-card traversal) and adapters.rs (icon-tile measurements) inform scripts/design-inspector.mjs and its replay fixtures. Changes: JavaScript reimplementation over jig's measured snapshots, all findings advisory, exact-rule waivers and intentional-theme records, functional selection/focus exclusions, no palette bans. The inspector contract records thresholds and narrower coverage; no full-engine parity is claimed. Third-party source was research data; no upstream code, installer, hooks, CLI or dependencies were executed.

There is no repository NOTICE file. Upstream NOTICE.md was inspected: it credits platform-design-skills for ios.md and android.md; neither is adapted here, so that unrelated notice is not redistributed. The original copyright and Apache licence are retained above and with the adapted inspector.

Adapted in our own words from Emil Kowalski's MIT-licensed skills: emil-design-eng, review-animations (including STANDARDS.md), choreograph, find-animation-opportunities, break-ui, and prototype (including PICKER.md). Second round: animate (including RECIPES.md), animation-vocabulary, apple-design, pick-ui-library, improve-animations (including AUDIT.md and PLAN-TEMPLATE.md), remove-animations, and animation-performance. All seven were read at revision c8a79627b59d72d764d6ab6f2c87c09a48169833, including every supporting file listed by that revision's repository tree. Raw files read 8 November 2026; nothing installed. Source-specific rules are linked above and in the mockup skill. The prototype picker informs full-size, instant switching; its fixed styling, copied wiring and width animation are not adopted. Local motion decisions and the coordinator's read-only draft were consulted; project names and private paths stay out of the reusable contract.

Not borrowed: ui-ux-pro-max-skill (large generic catalogues, unsourced rules); motion-canvas and the video skills (video, not interface motion); Infrasity animation-principles (unsourced, ease-in exits).

Second-round omissions: none of the seven skills omitted; skipped animate's marketing/hold/drag recipes and height/400 ms toast exceptions (scope and local budgets), vocabulary's verbatim-copy rule (own words), Apple's assets/glass mandate/bounce/physics constants/audio-haptics (project identity, restraint and no device work), picker's fixed dependency roster (project picks win), improve's agent/model dispatch and plan-approval workflow (bounded existing round), remove's blanket keyboard/loop cuts (local decisions win), and performance's guaranteed-acceleration/shadow-swap claims (must profile).
